note: Canonical angles are the block yaw relative to the camera: side 0 (faces screen right), front +90, back -90. The other half-circle is the mirror. See views/poser.ts for the selection rule.

side.note: Drawn right profile, re-cut by the side pipeline.

sideRear.note: The same profile with the garment redrawn as seen from behind. Used for the left-facing (mirrored) profile so chest prints are never shown mirrored.

front.note: Drawn front parts sheet. The trunk, arms and legs are true front drawings; the HEAD on that sheet is a three-quarter-front head, so a dead-on front face is a stand-in.

headStandIn.reason: The only front-ish head is drawn three-quarter, looking to its left.
headStandIn.replaceWith: A dead-on front head (hair/cap, both ears, neck stub) on the parts sheet.

back.reason: No back drawing exists. The tools reuse the front parts mirrored, with the shirt above the waist and the head flat-filled inside their own outlines.
back.replaceWith: A back parts sheet in the same layout as the front one: trunk from behind (shirt back, shorts seat), back of the head, two arms and two legs seen from behind.

threeQuarterFront.reason: No three-quarter body drawing exists. The front parts are narrowed by the projection (shoulder and hip width follow the 3D skeleton); the head is the true three-quarter head.
threeQuarterFront.replaceWith: A three-quarter-front parts sheet (45 degrees): trunk, near and far arm, near and far leg.

threeQuarterBack.reason: No three-quarter-back drawing exists. The back stand-in narrowed by the projection.
threeQuarterBack.replaceWith: A three-quarter-back parts sheet (135 degrees), same layout.
